jobs.title: Community Health Worker I
jobs.description:
WelbeHealth’s PACE program helps seniors stay in their homes and communities by providing medical care and community-based services. We like to do things a little differently, going the extra mile and making a difference in our participants’ lives.

The Community Health Worker I provides direct center and field-based support to PACE participants by addressing Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) needs and reducing barriers to accessing essential services. This role focuses on assisting participants with connections to community resources, supporting application completion for community programs, and ensuring participants are able to access services that support health, safety, and stability.

*This role is different because the Community Health Worker I at WelbeHealth:*

Works within an interdisciplinary team (IDT), receive ongoing professional development, and have a direct impact on improving outcomes for older adults through both individual support and community-level solutions
Plays a critical role in supporting a growing, mission-driven healthcare organization, ensuring vulnerable seniors feel supported and have access to high-quality care

* We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:
*

Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
401K savings + match
Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus
And additional benefits!

On The Day-to-day, You Will

Provide direct participant support to address SDoH needs through home visits, outreach, and in-person assistance focused on accessing essential services and resources
Connect participants to established community resources (e.g., housing supports, food insecurity resources, utility assistance, caregiver support, transportation resources, etc.) and follow up to support access, eligibility verification, and utilization
Assist participants with completing and submitting applications for identified community resources and community-based programs
Support Social Workers in discharge planning by supplying applicable community resource information during PACE disenrollment
Support participants with complex needs through ongoing engagement, resource connection support, and barrier resolution that directly impacts health outcomes and quality of life
Collaborate with Social Workers, ECAs, PELs, and the broader IDT to reinforce participant-centered care plans and ensure coordinated resource support
Assist with completing grievances, appeals, incident reports, APS reports, and other quality or compliance-related requirements as needed

Job Requirements Include

High school diploma or equivalency required
Associate’s degree in social work, human services, social science, or relevant field preferred
Reliable means of transportation
Strong knowledge of community-based services and resource navigation
Experience working with older adults or vulnerable populations is a plus
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

We are seeking a Community Health Worker I that ideally has experience working with frail or elderly populations. If you’re ready to join a team that values both its participants and team members, we’d love to hear from you!

Compensation consists of base salary plus bonus. WelbeHealth offers a competitive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and a broad range of additional benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and relevant qualifications.

Compensation Offering

$23.31—$29.66 USD

COVID-19 Vaccination Policy

At WelbeHealth, our mission is to unlock the full potential of our vulnerable seniors. In this spirit, please note that we have a vaccination policy for all our employees and proof of vaccination, or a vaccine declination form will be required prior to employment. WelbeHealth maintains required infection control and PPE standards and has requirements relevant to all team members regarding vaccinations.

* Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
*

At WelbeHealth, we embrace and cherish the diversity of our team members, and we're committed to building a culture of inclusion and belonging. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. People seeking employment at WelbeHealth are considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information or characteristics (or those of a family member), pregnancy or other status protected by applicable law.

Please ensure your application is being submitted through a WelbeHealth sponsored site only. Our emails will come from @welbehealth.com email addresses. You will never be asked to purchase your own employment equipment. You can report suspected scam activity to [fraud.report@welbehealth.com](mailto:fraud.report@welbehealth.com)

Attalon is a leading technology partner to the global aerospace and defense industry, specializing in the physics of light and heat. This role requires managing cross-functional teams, coordinating multiple projects, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals while maintaining budget, schedule, and quality standards. The Program Manager VI will serve as a key liaison between stakeholders, including engineering, production, supply chain, and executive leadership, to facilitate communication and decision-making. Technical knowledge of manufacturing processes and quality standards allows the manager to make informed decisions and drive improvements. Preferred skills such as Lean and Six Sigma methodologies enhance the ability to identify inefficiencies and implement process improvements, while certifications and advanced degrees contribute to strategic thinking and credibility in managing large-scale initiatives.

Masters of Social Work (MSW) with experience working in a foster care program preferred. Child Welfare Training Institute (CWTI) training preferred. Knowledge Requirements: Computer and software applications (Windows, MS Office, Internet applications, etc.) necessary to perform the duties of the position. Principles and practices of social work, including the NASW Code of Ethics. Michigan Department of Health and Human Services policies and procedures. Family and child dynamics. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, other agencies, and the public. Exercise professional judgment in making decisions. Handle sensitive and confidential situations and documentation. Attend training and maintain necessary certifications and licenses. Maintain a Michigan drivers license and driving record that allows the operation of an agency or personal vehicle for agency business or to transport clients as needed. IV. As a Case Manager/Child Safety Specialist
, you’ll:

Work full-time, 40 hours a week on-site/in field; alternative work hours may be required
Respond to allegations of child abuse or neglect
Conduct interviews and assess child safety
Work with families in their homes and in the community
Coordinate services and develop case plans
Attend court hearings and prepare professional reports

Remain calm in stressful situations; understand diverse family systems and cultural backgrounds; and show empathy while maintaining professional boundaries
Provide strong attention to detail

Bachelor’s or master’s degree earned from an institution accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education (conferred transcripts); OR 4 years as an Arizona Department of Child Safety Case Aide

The ability to obtain and maintain a valid Department of Public Safety Level One Fingerprint Clearance Card
Work history, Central Registry and Public Record will be considered
Successfully complete the 22 weeks of in person classroom and field training program

Counseling, conflict resolution, and intervention techniques.

Confidentiality and ethical decision-making
Behavioral indicators of abuse/neglect, separation, and loss

Upon successful completion of the Arizona Department of Child Safety 22-week training program: $22.59/hour
After one year of Arizona Department of Child Safety Specialist service: $24.11
After two years of Arizona Department of Child Safety Specialist service: $25.96
After three years of Arizona Department of Child Safety Specialist service: $27.66

Placement within the DCS Specialist step pay plan may include credit for qualifying years of service as an OCWI Investigator Senior, in addition to prior DCS Specialist experience, in accordance with agency policy.

The CORE program includes seven weeks of classroom training within the 22-week program. Classroom sessions occur in one- to three-week blocks and are held in midtown Phoenix. Eligible hires receive hotel accommodations, as well as meal and mileage reimbursements during required in-person training.

A supportive retirement plan through the Arizona State Retirement System (ASRS)
10 paid holidays annually and generous vacation and sick leave
Paid Parental Leave Program (must meet the criteria)

Program Leadership –
Drives implementation of multiple, complex program initiatives as the single accountable program manager, working closely with cross-functional teams and resources to achieve program/project milestones within established timeframes, directing roughly forty interdependent sub-projects and twelve portfolios from chartering through operational handover.

Governance & Controls –
Manages the utilization of PMO standards and methodologies — including the PMO operating model, lifecycle/tollgates, project charter, change-control processes, review and sign-off, integrated master schedule, RAIDA (risks, actions, issues, decisions, assumptions) cadence, decision logs, and dashboards — ensuring transparent, disciplined execution.

Execution & Delivery –

Oversees operational readiness, workforce and site transition, knowledge transfer, and formal handover to operations; removes obstacles and impediments to ensure business and operational objectives are met, confirming demonstrated stable output and supply continuity before legacy ramp-down.

Documentation & Compliance –
Owns quality control of program deliverables and artifacts and the creation and maintenance of comprehensive program documentation, ensuring traceability, alignment with PMO standards, and compliance with company policies and procedures.

Tracks and reports program KPIs (schedule, cost, risk burn-down, milestone achievement, stakeholder engagement); identifies and applies best practices and needed process improvements, provides coaching and feedback to project owners and key stakeholders, and acts as a model and champion for continuous-improvement and change-management practices.
